kit.name: ELEGOO UNO R3 Super Starter Kit

identity.canonical_name: 9V battery snap connector with 2.1mm barrel jack plug
identity.manufacturer: ELEGOO (kit private label); the underlying connector design is generic and sold unbranded by many electronics vendors
identity.manufacturer_part_number: not confirmed, ELEGOO does not publish a distinct part number for this accessory
generic_equivalents: Adafruit 9V battery clip with 5.5mm/2.1mm barrel plug (PID 80)
identity.package: cable, battery snap connector molded to a coaxial barrel plug

function.one_sentence_plain_english: A short cable that snaps onto a 9V battery on one end and plugs into the UNO board's round power socket on the other end, so the board can run without a computer.
function.what_it_is_used_for: Powers the Arduino UNO R3 from a 9V battery instead of the USB cable, useful for portable or battery-powered projects.
function.how_it_works_briefly: The snap connector clips onto the two terminals on top of a standard 9V battery, one terminal shaped smaller than the other so it only clips on one way. Wires run from the snap to a cylindrical barrel plug, 2.1mm on the inside and 5.5mm on the outside, wired so the center pin is positive. That plug pushes into the UNO's DC power jack.

pinout.name: positive (+)
pinout.role: carries battery positive through to the barrel plug's center pin
pinout.notes: On the 9V battery, this is the smaller of the two snap studs.

pinout.name: negative (-) / ground
pinout.role: carries battery negative through to the barrel plug's outer sleeve
pinout.notes: On the 9V battery, this is the larger of the two snap studs.

pins.pin_1_identification: The battery-end caps are molded plastic sized differently, like the battery's own terminals, so the snap only clips on one way. On the barrel-plug end, positive is the thin center pin and negative is the outer metal sleeve around it, the standard center-positive layout confirmed on the generic equivalent (Adafruit PID 80).

electrical.operating_voltage: 9V nominal, set by the battery clipped on, not by the cable
electrical.absolute_max_voltage: not_applicable, this is a passive wire; the limit is whatever the connected battery and the UNO's power jack allow, not the cable itself
electrical.typical_current: not confirmed for ELEGOO's exact cable or for the generic equivalent part checked; a 9V battery itself can only safely supply small currents (well under 1A) so treat this as light duty
electrical.max_current: not confirmed, no source found rates this connector's wire for a maximum current
electrical.logic_level: not_applicable, this is a power cable and carries no logic signal

key_specs.connector_type: 9V battery snap clip wired to a coaxial DC barrel plug

visual_identification.shape_and_size: A short two-wire cable. One end has two small rectangular plastic caps sized to snap onto the two terminals on top of a 9V battery. The other end has a small black cylindrical plug, roughly the size of a pencil eraser, that pushes straight into a round socket.
visual_identification.color_and_markings: Usually plain black wire insulation and black plastic housings; some versions use red insulation for the positive wire and black for negative.
visual_identification.printed_text_to_look_for: Typically none, this is a small unbranded accessory with no printed markings.
easily_confused_with: The barrel-plug end of a wall-wart AC power adapter (same size plug, but that one is not attached to a battery snap)
The ELEGOO Power Supply Module's own power input cable

example_connections.uno_pin: DC power jack (round barrel socket next to the USB port)

required_extra_parts: A 9V battery. Whether ELEGOO ships an actual battery in the box or only this connector could not be confirmed for certain, see confidence.notes.
wiring_to_uno.arduino_library: none, this is a power connection only and needs no code

hazards: Touching the barrel plug's center pin and outer sleeve together while a battery is clipped on shorts the battery, which can make it hot

If the cable or the board's jack were ever wired backward, reversed polarity could damage the UNO, though standard manufactured parts are keyed to the same center-positive convention so this is unlikely in normal use
handling_notes: Unclip the battery when the project is not in use to save battery life
Do not leave a swollen, leaking, or damaged 9V battery clipped in
common_mistakes: Assuming this line item always includes an actual 9V battery in the box, some kit revisions ship the connector only
Treating it as a generic 2-wire jumper instead of the specific snap-to-barrel adapter it is molded as

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: UNO board does not power on from the battery
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: dead battery, snap connector clipped on backward, or the barrel plug not fully seated in the jack
symptoms_and_causes.check: Measure the battery with a multimeter and confirm the barrel plug clicks all the way into the UNO's jack

troubleshooting.how_to_test_with_a_multimeter: Set the multimeter to DC volts. With a 9V battery clipped on, touch the red probe to the barrel plug's center pin and the black probe to its outer sleeve. A good cable and battery should read close to positive 9V; a negative reading with the same probe placement would mean the wiring is reversed.

sources.title: 9V battery clip with 5.5mm/2.1mm plug, Adafruit product 80

confidence.notes: Two attempts to fetch ELEGOO's own product/tutorial pages returned no usable kit-contents text (one page had no relevant content, the tutorial blog and a Tayda/Jameco spec page both returned HTTP 403), and an Amazon listing fetch returned only page scaffolding with no visible bullet text. All electrical and physical specs here are backed by a generic equivalent part (Adafruit PID 80), not ELEGOO's exact private-labeled cable, since no ELEGOO-specific datasheet exists for this accessory. Price is single-unit retail for that generic equivalent, not an ELEGOO-branded standalone sale (ELEGOO does not sell this piece separately).
